newsitem.title: USA: Pfizer rises on Q4, '97 outlook.
newsitem.headline: Pfizer rises on Q4, '97 outlook.

text.p: Shares in Pfizer Inc rose on Thursday after the pharmaceutical company posted fourth quarter results that met Wall Street expectations and pointed to strong growth in 1997.
"It's a really good report," said David Maris at Aros Securities. "Expectations are so high on the company but they're meeting them."
Pfizer rose 5/8 to 87-1/2 in initial trading after a delayed opening on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.77 a share, up from $0.65 a year ago.
Pfizer's net income rose 23 percent to $504 million.

Pfizer also said it expects double-digit growth in sales and net income in 1997. Pfizer reported 1996 earnings of $2.99 a share on sales of $11.3 billion, compared to $2.50 a share on sales of $10.0 billion in 1995.

The company said that it also expects a 20 percent increase, to $2 billion, in research and development spending in 1997. It also said the launches of Aricept, a treatment for Alzheimer's disease patients, and the cholesterol-lowerer Lipitor were "imminent."
Analysts said the statements were in line with previous comments from the company but served to confirm Wall Street's upbeat outlook on the drug maker.
"There aren't very many multi-billion-dollar multi-nationals that are growing net income 23 percent," Rodman and Renshaw's James Keeney said.
Strong sales of the heart drug Norvasc and the antibiotic Zithromax were helping drive Pfizer's earnings, he said.
Other drug shares showed strength on Thursday, with Bristol-Myers Squibb Co up 1-1/8 to 119-3/8, Merck and Co Inc up one to 84-3/8 and Schering-Plough Corp up 1-1/2 to 70-3/4.
